Original source account: For a one-dimensional conservation law, each component of q is a conserved density. For any two fixed spatial points x₁ and x₂, the time derivative of the integral of q from x₁ to x₂ equals f(q(x₁,t)) minus f(q(x₂,t)); the total amount changes only through endpoint flux. This is the explicit balance and physical interpretation in raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, equation (1.10) and its following explanation. The surrounding text allows vector states and nonlinear fluxes (raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, definition of q; raw PDF pages 25–26, printed pages 3–4, Section 1.1). It conditions derivation of the differential PDE on sufficient smoothness and asserts that integral conservation remains fundamental at discontinuities, but does not specify the exact analytic interpretation needed there (raw PDF page 26, Section 1.1.2, continuing on raw PDF page 27).
